cues.en: Datawhale EAI builds a reproducible AMD Physical AI stack
across dexterous hands, household manipulation, simulation, and rendering.
The film begins with a real task outcome,
then follows the evidence back to the code and the machine that produced it.
One evidence contract follows data, policy, physics, and proof
across the complete project.
Every result keeps its task definition, model, seed, environment,
video, metrics, and checksum together,
so the viewer can move from a beautiful frame to a reproducible run.
RoboCasa three sixty-five gives us a household manipulation benchmark
with fixed tasks, seeds, videos, and a mobile observation contract.
The kitchen scenes make the target concrete:
reach, grasp, transport, open, place, and recover.
The official task boundary stays visible throughout every household trace.
Long-horizon success traces make the full action sequence inspectable.
Packing and restocking show why the trajectory matters:
the robot must keep contact, preserve the object,
complete several sub-actions, and finish in the correct state.
Shorter attempts move quickly to the next evidence clip, keeping the story focused.
DexJoCo brings contact-rich dexterous tasks into the same protocol,
with native JAX running on AMD ROCm.
Bimanual assembly, Hanoi, and microwave manipulation
put the hand in the difficult part of the problem:
precise contact, coordinated fingers, and long action sequences.
These are the success traces worth giving time to, because the outcome is easy to inspect.
Each result carries its own protocol and denominator.
Official seeds set the benchmark,
recovery searches answer a separate engineering question,
and single-task diagnostics explain a specific behavior.
The film keeps every claim attached to its source while moving at a steady pace.
Every line remains ready for review and reuse.
The evidence contract is simple:
data becomes policy, policy meets physics, and every result becomes proof.
Demonstrations are converted into a standard dataset,
the policy is trained or fine-tuned on AMD,
the simulator executes the action loop,
and the evaluator records stage outcomes.
The final package joins code, a command, a video, a JSON record, and a hash.
DISCOVERSE preserves expert paths, policy experiments,
multi-view rendering, and MP4 output after migration.
The same scene can be inspected from the task camera,
an external view, and a diagnostic angle.
That makes migration visible:
the environment still resets,
the expert path still runs,
the policy loop still produces evidence,
and the video remains useful to a learner.
Three-D Gaussian Splatting and dynamic replay
turn the renderer itself into visible migration evidence.
Rendering is a first-class AMD path:
point assets, camera motion, lighting, camera path,
and replay output travel through the same reproducibility checks
as the policy, with detail.
ROCm versions, GPU identity, memory, throughput, training time,
JSON, MP4, and SHA travel with every result.
We record the execution path explicitly:
PyTorch or JAX, the HIP runtime, the selected GPU,
the memory footprint, the training command,
the evaluation command,
and the exact artifact hash.
That is how an AMD port becomes evidence rather than a claim.
Success leads the story,
but the source evidence stays attached behind it:
code, videos, metrics, and checksums.
The strongest clips earn a complete moment on screen.
Shorter clips answer one question and move on.
The website then opens the deeper layer:
notebooks, weights, raw evaluation records, environment notes,
and the commands used to reproduce each result.
On AMD, PAC-MAN predictive control turns perception into a whole-body dodge.
Unitree G1 tracks the projectile, predicts its path,
and coordinates its whole body to preserve clearance
as the threat crosses the scene in real time on AMD.
The closing traces then map navigation, contact, release, and recovery into targets.
Each stage stays linked to the video and the next control decision.
Build it, run it, and show the proof
through code, notebooks, weights, reports, videos, and reproducible commands.
Datawhale-EAI brings the result to AMD ROCm as an open, inspectable project:
the next person should be able to run the command, see the motion,
and understand the success and the next step.
